title: Advanced Uses for Lists
bullets: Creating multiple separate, yet related lists.

title: Parallel Lists
paragraphs: Parallel lists are separate lists where values at the same index are related to one another.
They are useful when you want to keep different types of related data in separate collections.
The lists must stay in the same order so that matching indices continue to represent the same item.

title: Creating Related Lists
paragraphs: Two (or more) related lists can be created by storing matching data at the same index in each list.
For example, one list can store student names while another stores their grades.
Index 0 in both lists refers to the same student, index 1 refers to the next student, and so on.

title: Traversing with Indices
paragraphs: Parallel lists can be traversed using indices so the same position can be accessed in both lists.
A range() loop can generate each valid index.
This works well when you need direct control over the index.
code:
names = ["Alex", "Sam", "Jordan"]
grades = [82, 91, 76]

for i in range(len(names)):
    print(f"{names[i]}: {grades[i]}")

title: Traversing with enumerate()
paragraphs: The enumerate() function provides both the index and the value from a list during traversal.
The index can then be used to access the related value in another list.
This can make index-based traversal easier to read.
code:
names = ["Alex", "Sam", "Jordan"]
grades = [82, 91, 76]

for i, name in enumerate(names):
    print(f"{name}: {grades[i]}")

title: Traversing with zip()
paragraphs: The zip() function combines matching values from multiple lists during traversal.
This allows related values to be accessed directly without manually working with indices.
zip() is often the simplest option when you only need the matching values.
code:
names = ["Alex", "Sam", "Jordan"]
grades = [82, 91, 76]

for name, grade in zip(names, grades):
    print(f"{name}: {grade}")

title: Wrap Up
bullets: Parallel lists store related values at matching indices.
Keep list order aligned so matching positions refer to the same item.
Traverse related lists with indices, enumerate() or zip().
